object_description: rotated extension building with a lowered hall and alternating shed roofs
design_condition: the extension is turned to mirror the orientation of the adjacent residential buildings and the high school, and the hall is lowered to limit its height and integrate the large volume into the residential context

positive: Turning the extension mirrors the orientation of the residential buildings and the high school
This simple strategy creates an urban reference to the high school
It gives a good spatial connection with the outdoor spaces of the neighbourhood
It creates a clear access situation
Lowering the hall and limiting its height integrates the large building into the residential context
Despite its size the volume is so cleverly placed that it hardly disrupts the neighbourhood
The rotation creates an interesting forecourt where the main entrance is clearly visible
The entrance is aligned with the existing hall and appears equivalent to its access
Bicycle parking is sensibly located on the spacious forecourt next to the main entrance
A seating element and accessible parking are also on the forecourt
The usable spaces are arranged on two sides oriented to the outside and the hall
The building can be read from outside as school and sports hall thanks to the fine staging
Both uses are reached from the access zone via separate stairs regardless of opening times
The weight room is operationally optimally located directly adjacent to the hall
The hall has windows and skylights and a calm interior atmosphere with sufficient daylight
The planned spatial structure allows the desired flexibility in arranging studio and classrooms
Alternating shed structures light halls and school rooms zenithally
They refer to the living environment in their external appearance
The slat principle allows the glass proportion to be adapted to orientation and daylight needs
The energy standard, system separation, ecology and sustainability requirements are adequately described
Building technology is consistently planned and installed openly, with photovoltaics on the roof
Fire protection, escape route and building physics requirements are planned comprehensibly
The clear site planning concept and the appropriate architectural design are convincing in some areas
negative: The new building has a very large footprint at the expense of the surrounding areas
The many parking spaces north of the hall are less well located
There are no shady trees, so the large surface would heat up significantly in summer
Additional outdoor uses are arranged in residual spaces at the plot boundary
The parking occupies almost the entire central outdoor area with narrow, winding entrances
The materialisation of the covering surfaces is unclear and contradictory between text and image
Percolating coverings are only used selectively, so much water must be collected and drained
The proportion of green space is very low, negative ecologically and micro-climatically
No information is given on the types of new plantings and seeds
The lighting of the rooms in the inner layer is judged insufficient
Individual point skylights lead to uneven lighting in the hall, disadvantageous for sport
The interior layer offers views into the hall that are not operationally desirable
The roof construction is judged complex and the statics at the roof valleys are unsolved
The wooden slats in front of the glazing are unsuitable due to shadows and cleaning
The situation concept only creates small, insufficiently usable remaining outdoor areas
A clear outdoor design concept and user-friendly environmental planning are missing
There is no coherent parking solution
